chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, and I was present, about a man who became sexually impure (junub) in his garment and sweated in it. He said: 'I do not see a problem with it.' It was said to him: 'He sweats to such an extent that if he wished to wring it, he could wring it (and sweat would drip).' He said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) frowned in the face of the man and said: If you refuse (that it is pure), then (he should take) a little water to sprinkle it with.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the purity of clothes if a person in janabah sweats in them?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on clothing soiled by sweat during *janabah*, distinguishing between negligible moisture and copious sweat that can be wrung out. While the initial ruling permits the garment, the Imam’s furrowing brow and subsequent instruction to sprinkle water highlight the scholarly preference for *ihtiyat* (precaution) in matters of ritual purity to ensure the validity of prayer. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that while minor impurities do not invalidate the garment, removing them through sprinkling (*nathr*) is a recommended act to maintain spiritual cleanliness.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked, and I was presence, about a man who came to be with sexual impurity in his clothes, and he sweated in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see a problem with it’. So it was said, ‘He sweated to such an extent that had he so desired to wring it, would have wrung it (and sweat would have dripped from it)’. He (the narrator) said: ‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> frowned in the face of the man and said: ‘If you refuse, so (he should take) something from the water to sprinkle with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once was asked, when I was present, about a man who has experienced sexual relation and perspires in his clothes. He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not find anything harmful in it.’ Someone then said, ‘His perspiration is so much that he can wring it out.’ He (the narrator) said that abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then glared at the man’s face and said, ‘If you do not mind, in such case, he can use some water to wash it away.’””
